images.filename: North Shore Trip - Fall 2012 - Split Rock Clockworks (8061058683).jpg
images.caption:
Split Rock is unusual in that the clockworks that was originally used to rotate the giant lens is not only still in existence, but it has also been restored and continues to rotate the lens today.

Clockworks are like a giant grandfather clock.  A counterweight drops down the center of the tower and causes the clocksworks to spin, which causes the lens to turn.

images.filename: Split Rock Lighthouse - North Shore of Lake Superior.jpg
images.caption:
Split Rock Lighthouse — located along the North Shore of Lake Superior, near Two Harbors, Minnesota.

Shipwrecks from a mighty 1905 November gale prompted this rugged landmark’s construction. Completed by the U.S. Lighthouse Service in 1910, Split Rock Light Station was soon one of Minnesota’s best known landmarks.
Restored to its 1920s appearance, the lighthouse offers a glimpse of lighthouse life in this remote and spectacular setting.

images.filename: North Shore Trip - Split Rock at Sunrise (20397681719).jpg
images.caption: Split Rock Lighthouse at sunrise.  Split Rock is on the North Shore of Lake Superior and sits on a 120 foot sheer cliff overlooking the lake.  If you look closely in the lantern, you'll see the glinting of light sparkling on the lens.  The lens is the original fresnel lens that was installed when the light was put in service over 100 years ago.
images.alt: Split Rock Lighthouse at sunrise.  Split Rock is on the North Shore of Lake Superior and sits on a 120 foot sheer cliff overlooking the lake. images.caption: North Shore Trip - Split Rock at Sunrise
images.alt: North Shore Trip - Split Rock at Sunrise

images.caption:
It was a misty, hazy morning which muted the colors and the sky once the sun rose.  It is still a spectacular view.

This lighthouse is one of my favorite places in the world to visit.  I don't really understand why -- but something about this lighthouse feels like home to me.
